introduction_markdown: Time allowed: two and a half hours. Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour and Section II in 1 1/2 hours; you are advised to divide your time accordingly. In Section II answer EITHER the a, b and c OR the d, e and f of each question. For your guidance the approximate mark for each part of a question is indicated in brackets. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you are advised to show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Where necessary, assume: the acceleration of free fall, $g = 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}}$; the speed of light in air, $c = 3\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the charge on an electron, $e = 1.6\times10^{-19}\,\mathrm{C}$. Calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown:
A student places her mouth at one end of a U-shaped tube containing water of density $1000\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$. She sucks and causes a displacement as shown in figure 2.

![fig-1](gce-ol-physics-2025-p2-officiel-cameroun_exercice_4_fig_1.png)

*Figure 2*

figures.legende: Figure 2: U-shaped tube open at both ends (arms A-B on the left, D-C on the right). The water surface B in the left arm is 10 cm above the bottom of the tube; the water surface C in the right arm is 13 cm above the bottom.

incertitudes: Aucun corrigé officiel : toutes les réponses sont rédigées pour ce lot (modèle de réponse complet) ; les réponses qualitatives (définitions, listes, rédaction d'expériences) sont à relire par un enseignant de physique avant mise en avant.

Le sujet n'imprime pas de total par question : `points` de l'exercice = somme des points imprimés bloc par bloc ; pour la question 7, 8 et 9 de la Section II, c'est le total d'un seul jeu de sous-parties (a+b+c = d+e+f = 20), les deux jeux étant au choix.
Scan avec fantômes du verso (texte miroir qui transparaît) : relu en image sur la page nettoyée, aucun mot illisible dans les énoncés retenus.

Figure 2 : le sujet n'indique pas l'extrémité où l'élève aspire. Lecture retenue : on aspire dans le bras où le niveau est le plus haut, donc en D (niveau C à 13 cm, niveau B à 10 cm). Les hauteurs 10 cm et 13 cm sont mesurées depuis le bas du tube (pointillés du bas).
Constante donnée dans l'énoncé de la question 4 : masse volumique de l'eau 1000 kg m^-3, utilisée avec g = 10 m s^-2 de la page de garde.

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) Using a letter on the diagram, state where she places her mouth. *[1 mark]*

(ii) Explain why the displacement occurs. *[2 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
**(i)** She places her mouth at **D**, the end of the arm in which the water level is higher (surface C).

**(ii)** Sucking at D removes air and **lowers the air pressure above the water surface C**. The atmospheric pressure acting on the water surface B at the open end A is now **greater** than the pressure above C. This pressure difference pushes the water down in arm A and up in arm D until the extra pressure of the water column of height $h$ between the two levels balances it (pressure at the same level in the same liquid must be equal).

questions.enonce_markdown: Determine the pressure difference caused by the sucking. *[3 marks]*
questions.corrige_markdown:
The pressure difference equals the pressure of the column of water between the two levels:

$$\Delta p = \rho g h$$

Height difference: $h = 13\,\mathrm{cm} - 10\,\mathrm{cm} = 3\,\mathrm{cm} = 0.03\,\mathrm{m}$.

$$\Delta p = 1000\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}} \times 10\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-2}} \times 0.03\,\mathrm{m} = 300\,\mathrm{Pa}$$

**The pressure difference caused by the sucking is $300\,\mathrm{Pa}$** ($300\,\mathrm{N\,m^{-2}}$).

Trap: do not use 13 cm or 10 cm alone; only the difference between the two levels matters.
